data.name: French Polynesia
data.summary: French Polynesia has no general personal income tax. Gains on securities and income from foreign assets are untaxed for individuals. Local dividends bear IRCM plus a 5% solidarity levy (CST). Real estate gains are taxed at 50% within 5 years, then on a sliding scale to 0% after 10 years. There is no wealth tax. Inheritance duties exist, but their rates for children could not be found, so the inheritance score is unverified.

regimes.name: Residence in French Polynesia
regimes.description: No general income tax. Separate levies hit specific income: CST on wages and pensions, IRCM + CST on distributions by local companies, and the real estate gains tax.
regimes.eligibility: Living in French Polynesia; no general income tax return. The DICP can only certify which local taxes a person is registered for.

capital_gains.summary: No tax on gains from securities for individuals (no general income tax). Real estate gains are taxed at 50% if the property was held under 5 years, then 20%, 16%, 12%, 8% and 4% in years 5-9, and 0% after 10 years (from 10 Dec 2024).

capital_gains.rate_basis: DICP: 'Il n'existe pas en Polynésie française d'impôt général sur l'ensemble des revenus.' The real estate scale is from the government's OpenFisca parameter (in force 10 Dec 2024), consistent with IEOM 2025 (50% under 5 years since 2022, disappears after 10 years). Real estate scored at 0 because the guide assumes a holding beyond every holding period. Headline 0.50 = the short-holding real estate rate.
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: Real estate: 50% under 5 years, 20% in year 5 falling 4 points a year to 0% from year 10.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Foreign assets untaxed (DICP: foreign rental income not taxable; no general income tax).

dividends.summary: Dividends from local companies are subject to IRCM (withheld and declared by the paying company) plus CST on investment income at 5%. Foreign dividends received directly by a resident are not taxed: there is no general income tax and IRCM applies to distributions by entities in French Polynesia.

dividends.withholding_outbound: IRCM plus 5% CST-RCM on distributions by local companies (IRCM does not apply to dividends paid to companies with their seat in French Polynesia, art. LP.178-1).
dividends.treaty_network: Only a tax agreement with France (1957); no treaties with the US or other countries.
dividends.holding_company_notes: Dividends to local companies are outside IRCM (art. LP.178-1).

inheritance.summary: Transfers on death are declared to and taxed by the Direction des affaires foncières (Recette-Conservation des hypothèques), which liquidates registration duties on 'mutations par décès'. The direct-line rates and allowances could not be found, so this metric is unverified: the JSON scores no duty, which may overstate how favourable French Polynesia is.

corporate.summary: Corporate income tax 25% (27% until 2022), plus a CSIS surcharge on large profits rising to 15% above XPF 400M (government OpenFisca parameters). Local investment tax credits (défiscalisation locale).

data.us_citizen_notes: No US treaty. A US citizen living in French Polynesia still pays full US federal tax on worldwide income and US estate tax; the local regime gives almost nothing to credit.

succession.name: French Polynesia
succession.summary: French civil law applies, so children have a protected share (the réserve) that a will cannot cut. A foreign resident cannot choose their national law, and the EU Succession Regulation does not apply. The Hague Trusts Convention is not in force for France.
succession.reserved_share: Children: 1/2 with one child, 2/3 with two, 3/4 with three or more (Code civil art 913); if no descendants, a surviving spouse 1/4 (art 914-1).
succession.foreign_law_note: The EU Succession Regulation does not apply in French Polynesia (an overseas country and territory). Under French common-law conflict rules, land follows the law of its location and movables the last domicile, so a resident cannot select national law (not verified from a Polynesian source).
succession.trust_note: The fiducie (Code civil arts 2011 ff.) is a statutory trust with narrow uses; its extension to French Polynesia was not verified. France has signed but not ratified the Hague Trusts Convention. Foundations: only charitable forms known in France; local availability not verified.
